technical.lead: Knight Institute and EFF join FMRB public-comment fight
technical.body: The Knight First Amendment Institute and Electronic Frontier Foundation file a Saturday-morning amicus letter joining the May 8 AI Policy Institute / R Street / Public Knowledge / Lawyers for Civil Justice coalition, arguing any pre-release notification regime relying on Defense Production Act Section 708 voluntary information-sharing authority must include at minimum a 60-day public comment window plus a documented reasoned-decision record per State Farm. Senator Mark Warner's office confirms the May 15 classified Frontier Model Review Board threshold briefing is now scheduled for 14:00 EDT in S-407 with NIST Director Laurie Locascio, the ODNI cyber lead, and a CISA Joint Cyber Defense Collaborative representative attending; Senator Todd Young's office adds Senator Jacky Rosen (Senate Cyber subcommittee chair) to the requesting cohort. White House OSTP signals via a Saturday press-pool note that the executive order draft remains in interagency review with no signing window before May 22.

technical.lead: South Korea and New Zealand extend cyber-eval reciprocity perimeter
technical.body: The Indo-Pacific cyber-evaluation reciprocity perimeter takes its first weekend extension. South Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission and the Ministry of Science and ICT publish a joint Saturday statement signaling intent to mirror the Singapore IMDA / Japan AISI memorandum-of-cooperation under a 90-day domestic-consultation window, with formal signature targeted for July; New Zealand's Government Communications Security Bureau confirms it will join Canada CCCS and Australia ASD ACSC as an observer with a Q3 2026 mirror commitment. The seventh-jurisdiction shape that the May 8 prediction window flagged now has named candidates. Mistral, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind reaffirm participation in the cohort under sharing-in-confidence terms; Mythos and GPT-5.5 remain the operational threshold, and the US recognition gap widens by one weekend.

technical.lead: Cerebras CBRS sell-side weekend reads consolidate Buy ratings
technical.body: Saturday post-trade reflection on the Cerebras CBRS debut: sell-side weekend coverage from Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and Citi hold their initiation Buy ratings with $165-$185 12-month targets, while Bernstein adds a Market-Perform initiation at $172 with sober commentary citing Saudi Aramco Digital MoU dependency as the top single-counterparty concentration risk. Cerebras CFO confirms in a Saturday investor-Q&A note that the 180-day lock-up expires October 28, 2026 (per the offering S-1 amendment 4) and that no early-release waiver is contemplated for OpenAI's $1B warrant package. Specialty arbitrage desks log first-day call-volume of approximately 38,400 contracts versus put-volume of 9,200, an unusually skewed flow consistent with the read that the SambaNova / Groq / Tenstorrent S-1 cohort behind Cerebras now treats CBRS as a reference rather than a hurdle.

technical.lead: Defender quarantines 24% of new MCP servers in 30 minutes
technical.body: MCP-server attack-surface telemetry consolidates over the weekend. Microsoft Defender for Cloud publishes a weekend supplemental note documenting that the May 7 MCP-server threat-detection module GA has now quarantined 24% of net-new MCP servers seen on Defender-protected estates within the first 30 minutes, up from the 19% reported Friday. Cisco-Astrix MCP-server identity gateway (co-branded with Defender XDR plus Microsoft Agent 365 audit ledger) hits 740 enterprise-tenant deployments inside its first 48 hours of availability. Sysdig Threat Research separately publishes a weekend addendum to the joint Adversa AI / Wiz / Sysdig telemetry showing the median time-from-MCP-server-provisioning to first credential-extraction-attempt has fallen to 19 minutes on unprotected estates, versus 4.3 hours on Defender-protected tenants. Cross-vendor agentic-AI control-plane visibility now exceeds 65% of new MCP-server provisioning events.

technical.lead: Unsloth router-only LoRA gets first community reproduction on RTX 6000 Ada
technical.body: Unsloth's router-only LoRA recipes get their first community reproduction over the weekend. A Saturday Hacker News front-page write-up documents a successful end-to-end Kimi K2.6 router-only LoRA run on a single RTX 6000 Ada workstation (96GB VRAM) following the Unsloth recipe published Friday, reporting 14% peak VRAM versus the full-LoRA-on-experts baseline and 76% accuracy recovery on the in-domain code-generation eval (within the 71-78% range from the Unsloth + Hugging Face joint preprint). Unsloth simultaneously ships a Saturday changelog adding two refinements: a quantization-aware router-only LoRA mode targeting 4-bit dynamic-bits-per-parameter that further trims peak VRAM by 19% on the Mixtral 8x22B and Llama 4 Behemoth recipes, and a Hugging Face PEFT compatibility shim that lets the router-only adapter export round-trip through the standard PEFT save/load pipeline without a custom loader.
